instruction: In the BoomerangSales spreadsheet, add a new column G with header 'Retail Price'. Use VLOOKUP to fill in the retail price for each product from the Retail Price sheet.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to calculate revenue using VLOOKUP from Retail Price sheet. Added 'Revenue' header in H1 and tried writing a VLOOKUP formula in H2, but got #N/A error. Spent 40+ turns trying to fix the formula by clicking various cells and re-entering formulas, but never succeeded. No pivot table was created.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate between sheets, click on cells, type text headers and values, attempt formula entry. Demonstrated understanding of spreadsheet layout and column structure.
metadata.failure_analysis: Model failed at constructing a correct VLOOKUP formula. The #N/A error suggests incorrect range reference or column index. The model kept retrying the same broken approach rather than debugging the formula parameters.
metadata.task_rationale: Isolates the VLOOKUP step from the original task. Instead of computing revenue (VLOOKUP + multiply + discount), this only requires the VLOOKUP itself, reducing complexity. Partial credit rewards header placement and each correct price lookup.
metadata.explanation: Task requires adding header 'Retail Price' in G1 and VLOOKUP formulas in G2:G36 referencing the Retail Price sheet. Getter reads G1 header and G2:G36 values. Metric gives 20% for header, 80% proportional to correct price values.

scoring_breakdown.values: 0.80 - Proportional to number of correct VLOOKUP prices in G2:G36

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads G1 header and G2:G36 values from column 7 (G) using openpyxl with data_only=True, which properly reads computed VLOOKUP results rather than formula strings.

Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule' — directly accesses expected.get('expected_header'), expected.get('expected_values'), expected.get('tolerance') without incorrectly nesting into expected['rules'].
Postconfig properly activates the window and saves the file (Ctrl+S) before the getter reads it, ensuring computed values are persisted to disk.
Both instruction requirements are covered: header check (20% weight) and VLOOKUP value correctness (80% weight with per-row partial credit).
Partial credit scoring logic is well-designed — proportional credit for each correct price value allows meaningful differentiation between partial and full completion.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Header check uses substring match (expected_header.lower() in header.lower()) instead of exact match. Consider using strip() + exact case-insensitive comparison for stricter verification.
Minor: Expected values (35 prices) cannot be independently verified without access to the actual Retail Price sheet data. If any expected value is wrong, correct completions would be penalized.
